title: Call a partial task a component
statement: Label a task that rehearses part of an exam format as a component, and give the format's own name only to items that meet its full current specification.
example: One course could not host a full document-based question in its first unit, because the official range begins in 1754.
detail: An audit of an AP history course found that a three-document set for its first period could be mistaken for an exam-aligned document-based question, although the official range for that format begins in 1754. The course's design notes hold that calling such an exercise by the full format's name would make it look more advanced while weakening the measurement contract, and its assessment system records question family, instructional role, format fidelity and evidence state separately, so an item can be excellent guided practice without being an exam simulation. Its contract counts a partial or out-of-range document task as a component, never as a full item, and its verifier rejects copies in which components are mislabelled as full items.
against: A limit, not a counter: some exam properties cannot be reproduced inside one unit at all: "A real exam distributes the three required SAQs across different historical periods, which a Unit 1 checkpoint cannot reproduce." (grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz:apush/docs/UNIT1-VERTICAL-SLICE.md, line 46).

evidence.quote: Calling a three-document Period 1 exercise a DBQ would make the artifact look more advanced while weakening the measurement contract.
Unit 1 cannot host a full official-range DBQ, because the current DBQ range begins in 1754.
The assessment system separates question family, instructional role, format fidelity, and evidence state. A question can be excellent guided practice without being a full exam simulation.
This preserves the instructional progression while making the reviewer-facing count honest: full exam-family items and partial teaching exercises never share a label.
A partial or out-of-range document task; never counted as a full DBQ.
A Unit 1 document set could also be mistaken for an exam-aligned DBQ even though the official DBQ range begins in 1754.
